question.problem: A survey of adult citizens of a particular city showed that $32%$ of all females and  $5%$ of all males don't eat after $6$ p.m. $51%$ of the population are female. If a person who doesn't eat after $6$ p.m. is selected at random, what is the probability of them being male? Express your answer as a percentage to the nearest percent.
question.worked_solution:
Let $N$ be the event that a randomly selected person doesn't eat after $6$ p.m., and let $M$ be the event that they are male. Then, we require $P(M|N),$ which we can compute using Bayes' theorem.

$$
P(M|N)=\frac{P(N|M)P(M)}{P(N)}=\frac{P(N|M)P(M)}{P(N|M)P(M)+P(N|{M}^{′})P({M}^{′})}
$$

From the problem statement, we have the following:

- Since $32%$ of all females and  $5%$ of all males don't eat after $6$ p.m, we have

$$
P(N|M)=0.05,\,P(N|{M}^{′})=0.32.
$$

- Since $51%$ of the population are female, we have

$$
P(M)=1-0.51=0.49,\,P({M}^{′})=0.51.
$$

Therefore, using Bayes' theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(M|N) & =\frac{P(N|M)P(M)}{P(N|M)P(M)+P(N|{M}^{′})P({M}^{′})} \\  & =\frac{(0.05)(0.49)}{(0.05)(0.49)+(0.32)(0.51)} \\  & ≈13%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest percent.
